claims.text: The page /docs/support/provider-support-policy/ exists in the Pulumi docs (linked from the support index as 'Provider support policy').
Pulumi's provider support policy page describes how long Pulumi maintains each provider major version.
Some Pulumi providers receive long-term security updates, and the provider support policy page identifies which ones.
Pulumi focuses on actively supporting the latest released major version of the providers it maintains.
For a set of widely used providers, Pulumi also ships security updates for the previous major version for up to a year, or until the next major version is released, whichever comes first.
The page /docs/support/provider-support-policy/ exists and lists the covered providers and what a long-term support release contains.
Older major versions of Pulumi-maintained providers receive no patches at all.
The Pulumi Registry (/registry/) lists the current version for all providers maintained by Pulumi.
Pulumi does not automatically roll back changes during an update if an error occurs; it completes pending in-progress operations, then exits and reports the error.
`pulumi up --refresh` refreshes and applies desired state in a single step.
Experimental Pulumi features are always opt-in and can be enabled via `PULUMI_EXPERIMENTAL=true`.
Pulumi does not use the Terraform engine, but some Pulumi providers use Terraform schemas; Pulumi native providers map directly to cloud provider APIs and do not use Terraform schemas.
Pulumi Cloud manages a unique encryption key per stack to encrypt secrets, configurable to use a custom secrets provider.
Each major version of a Pulumi provider includes migration logic to smooth upgrade from the immediately previous major version.
Pulumi actively maintains the latest released major version of every provider it publishes.
For a set of widely used providers, Pulumi ships security updates for the previous major version for up to 12 months, or until the next major version is released, whichever comes first.
The providers receiving Pulumi long-term support updates are AWS, Azure Classic, Azure Native, Azure AD, Command, Docker Build, GCP, Kubernetes, TLS, and Vault.
Registry package pages exist at /registry/packages/ for aws, azure, azure-native, azuread, command, docker-build, gcp, kubernetes, tls, and vault.

Pulumi provider LTS releases ship High/Critical CVE security patches, including fixes for CVEs in the provider's code or direct dependencies and fixes for broken internal infrastructure on the LTS branch needed to ship them.

Pulumi provider LTS releases do not contain new upstream API versions, new resources or properties, performance improvements, non-security bug fixes, or compatibility with newer language runtime versions.
LTS providers remain compatible with the version of Pulumi engine they were frozen at unless security fixes require otherwise.
Exactly one long-term support major version exists per covered provider at any time.
When major N+1 ships, it becomes the new N, the old N becomes the new LTS major, and the previous LTS major reaches end of life the same day regardless of remaining 12-month window.
Within the LTS major, only the latest minor version receives patches; earlier minors are frozen.
Pulumi provider LTS releases are available through the same standard package registries as current-major releases but are tagged differently.
Customers pinning to a specific major version of a Pulumi provider automatically receive patch releases as they ship, and pinning to a major is recommended.
Older majors than the LTS version of a covered provider receive no patches; if v3 is newest, v2 is N-1 and v1 and earlier are end of life.
The current major (N) receives new features, new resources, bug fixes, security patches, dependency upgrades, and new upstream API versions until N+1 ships.
LTS (N-1) lasts up to 12 months from N's release, or until N+1 ships, and ships security updates in the provider's code or direct dependencies.
Versions N-2 and older are end of life and receive no updates.
The infrastructure FAQ page has a section 'what are the best practices for maintaining provider versions' at /docs/support/faq/infrastructure/.
Pages exist at /registry/ and /docs/support/getting-support/.
